beats.narration: IBM's Granite four point oh H Small: forty layers, only four of them attention. The rest are Mamba. What does that buy, and what does it cost?
beats.narration_text: Granite 4.0-H-Small: (1) show me where the 4 attention layers sit among 36 Mamba-2 layers, (2) explain why it needs no positional encoding, (3) compute KV-cache and state memory at 131,072 tokens — from config.json.

props.title: Granite 4.0, Mostly Mamba?
thesis: 36 of its 40 layers are Mamba-2 recurrences with a fixed-size state; only 4 are
attention. No position encoding anywhere — the recurrence carries word order.

roadmap.label: The layout

beats.narration: Thirty-six of the forty layers are Mamba two. Attention appears only at layers six, sixteen, twenty-six, and thirty-six. Every layer routes to ten of seventy-two experts, plus a shared one.

moves.label: MAMBA-2
moves.detail: 36 layers: a state-space recurrence with a fixed-size state.

moves.label: ATTENTION
moves.detail: Layers 6, 16, 26 and 36 only — 32 query heads, 8 KV heads.

moves.label: EXPERTS
moves.detail: Every layer: 10 of 72 routed experts, plus a shared expert.

props.keepNote: Row 1 is the bet: nine layers in ten never grow their memory.

beats.narration: Why no position encoding? Attention alone doesn't see order: shuffle the past, and the scores shuffle with it. Mamba updates its state token by token, so order is built in.
beats.narration_text: Why no position encoding? Attention alone doesn't see order: shuffle the past, and the scores shuffle with it. Mamba updates its state token by token, so order is built in.

props.heading: Why no position encoding?

moves.label: ATTENTION
moves.detail: A score is q · k — the same wherever the key sits. On its own, attention is order-blind.

moves.label: MAMBA-2
moves.detail: The state updates token by token, h ← A·h + B·x, so order is built in.

moves.label: READOUT
moves.detail: y = C·h: each output reads a state that saw the past in order.

moves.label: RESULT
moves.detail: The 4 attention layers skip RoPE: position_embedding_type nope.

props.keepNote: Row 2 is why it works: with Mamba carrying order, attention can drop position encoding.
props.source: Dao & Gu — Transformers are SSMs (Mamba-2), arXiv:2405.21060 §2.1 eq. 2 · ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-small config.json

beats.narration: The memory, at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. Four attention layers cache about two gigabytes. All forty as attention: over twenty-one. The Mamba state stays seventy-five megabytes, at any length.
beats.narration_text: The memory, at a hundred thirty-one thousand tokens. Four attention layers cache about two gigabytes. All forty as attention: over twenty-one. The Mamba state stays seventy-five megabytes, at any length.

props.heading: Memory at 131,072 tokens — GB, BF16
props.exception: The state stays small because it compresses — exact lookup of an old token rests on just 4 layers.
props.source: Computed from config.json: 4 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 × (K,V) · state 128 heads × 64 × 128 × 36

beats.narration: Verdict: mostly Mamba is accurate, thirty-six of forty layers, and the memory savings are real. But exact retrieval rests on four layers. Measure it before you trust it.
beats.narration_text: Verdict: mostly Mamba is accurate, thirty-six of forty layers, and the memory savings are real. But exact retrieval rests on four layers. Measure it before you trust it.

artifactLines: Layout: 36 Mamba-2 + 4 attention layers (6, 16, 26, 36), MoE throughout.
Position: none needed — the recurrence carries order.
Memory: ~2.1 GB KV at 131K vs ~21.5 GB all-attention, plus a fixed ~75 MB state.
Exact retrieval rests on 4 layers — measure it.

beats.narration: Your turn. Hide a six digit code in documents of four, thirty-two, and a hundred twenty-eight thousand tokens. Compare with all-attention. Where does the hybrid start to miss?
beats.narration_text: Compare Granite 4.0-H-Small with a similar-size all-attention model. Hide one 6-digit code in documents of 4K, 32K and 128K tokens, then ask for it. Run 20 trials per length. Report exact-match accuracy and peak memory for both. Where does the hybrid start to miss?

props.command: Compare Granite 4.0-H-Small with a similar-size all-attention model. Hide one 6-digit code in documents of 4K, 32K and 128K tokens, then ask for it. Run 20 trials per length. Report exact-match accuracy and peak memory for both. Where does the hybrid start to miss?
